note.question: What determines its model identification and further propose a maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) for its calibration by real data?
note.overview: This paper incorporates a piecewise linear structure into the utility-price relationship of the classic multinomial logit (MNL) model and studies the associated operations problems such as estimation and pricing. The derived model is referred to as the piecewise MNL model. This paper studies its model identification and further propose a maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) for its calibration by real data.

conditions: The piecewise MNL model shares some similarity with the reference price MNL studied in Wang (2018), where the utility takes the form ui = αi β1pi + λ(r(S,p) pi)+ ν(pi r(S,p))+.
Here, r(S,p) is a prespecified function for reference price such as the average price r(S,p) = P i∈S pi=s.

This flexibility is shown to provide superior performance in empirical applications. (2) Product-specific heterogeneity: Although Wang (2018) assumes constant price sensitivity parameters (β1,λ,ν) and a uniform reference price for all products, our model accommodates product-specific parameters and thresholds.
The reference price r(S,p) serves as a known inflection point and is not part of the model parameter, making its model estimation same as a standard MNL.
